sentences.text: In respect of an accident which occurred on 03.10.2016, which resulted in the death of Musthaq Ahamedh, a claim petition was filed by his legal representatives.
2. In respect of the injuries suffered by an inmate of the goods auto, namely, Ameer John, another claim petition was filed.

3. The Tribunal has proceeded to award a sum of Rs.20,45,000/- as compensation to the death of Musthaq Ahamedh and a sum of Rs.2,50,000/- for the injuries suffered by an inmate of the goods auto, namely, B.K. Ameer John.
4.
The occurrence of the accident is not in dispute.
The insurer has, however, preferred an appeal contending that the Mustaq Ahamedh had himself contributed to the accident which occurred between his goods auto and the insured lorry.

However,
it is to be noticed here that the driver of this lorry has not been examined to establish that Mustaq Ahamedh was negligent.
6. It may also be pertinent to be noticed here that the police after investigation have also laid a chargesheet against the driver of the lorry.
In that view of the matter, the finding of the Tribunal that Mustaq Ahamedh was not negligent will have to be accepted.
Consequently, the appeal filed by insurer challenging the negligence will have to be dismissed.
7. As far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of Mustaq Ahamedh at Rs.15,000/-.
The insurer is in appeal, in the absence of any evidence the Tribunal would not have taken the income at Rs.15,000/-.
A perusal of NC: 2024:KHC:50717 the award indicates that no reasons have been given by the Tribunal for arriving the figure at Rs.15,000/-.

However, there is evidence on record to indicate that the claimant did possess a licence to drive auto and, therefore, the sum prescribed at Rs.9,500/- by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2016 cannot be automatically adopted.

8. In my view, having regard to the notional income fixed by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and also taking into consideration that Mustaq Ahamedh was having a licence to drive goods auto, it would be appropriate to treat the notional income at Rs.11,500/-.

9. Since the deceased was aged 40 years, future prospects of 25% requires to be added to the same,
which makes his income to be Rs.14,375/- (Rs.11,500/- + Rs.2,875/-). Since the deceased had NC:
2024:KHC:50717 six dependants, 1/3rd requires to be deducted from the same, which makes his income to be Rs.9,583/-.
10. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.17,24,940/- (Rs.9,583/- X 12 X '15' ) towards 'loss of dependency'.
B K Ameer John vs The Manager on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136974259/
6 11. The claimants would also be entitled to Rs.48,400/-
each towards loss of love and affection, which would be Rs.2,90,400/- (Rs.48,400/- X 6 members).
They are also entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/- towards miscellaneous expenses.
12. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.20,51,640/- as against Rs.20,45,000/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
13. As far as the compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- awarded to the injured - claimant, it is noticed that the Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 5%. It is noticed that the claimant has suffered - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:50717 severe crush injury to the left foot with fractures to 5th, 2nd and 3rd metatarsal bone, severe facial injury with facial bone fracture. In my view, in light of these facts, it would be appropriate to assess the whole body disability at 10%.
14.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant at Rs.10,000/-, since there was no evidence to that effect.

The same is just and proper Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,56,000/- (Rs.10,000/- X 12 X '13' X 10% disability) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
15.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.55,778/- towards 'medical expenses', the same is just and proper and is accordingly affirmed.
16. The Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards 'loss of amenities' and 'conveyance, food and nourishment charges'.

Since the claimant was hospitalsed for 8 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:50717 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively under the said heads.

17. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as one month, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as two months and consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- (Rs.10,000/- X 2 months) towards loss of earnings during laid up period.

18. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
